First listed 2025-10-06 · episode or wrap

Inside the AI Chip War: From Nvidia’s Dominance to Intel’s Turmoil | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 28

Stacy Rasgon separates the AI semiconductor boom from the weaker analog cycle, stresses NVIDIA's software ecosystem, and remains cautious about AMD and Intel. Eisman tests funding and return assumptions without declaring AI useless or predicting an imminent collapse. The clearest direct correction is that the announced NVIDIA investment in OpenAI was staged. The guest's claim that outsiders do not use TPUs is contradicted by Google's documented multi-year Anthropic relationship.

YouTube · 2025-10-06 ↗Substack · 2025-10-06 ↗
Claims are assessed individually. Empirical premises are not treated as successful forecasts. Unverified magnitudes and causal stories remain unresolved; subjective investment judgments are not assigned directional wins.

How he reasons here

  • Distinguish economic usefulness from returns on invested capital.
  • Separate cyclic digestion from a failed structural thesis.
  • Treat capex cuts as potentially late signals and monitor underlying use.
  • Do not infer equity value from TAM times assumed share.
  • Distinguish liquidity support from operating competitiveness.
